runs.answer: Inflation means prices rise over time. Think of money like a snack: when lots of people have extra money to spend, stores can charge more, because people keep buying. Also, making things can cost more, like gas or wages, so stores raise prices to cover it. That's why a candy bar that cost one dollar may cost more later.

Inflation means prices go up over time. Money also gets spread across more stuff, so each dollar buys a little less. Think of it like a bike that slowly gets more expensive every year. Lots of things, like wages, shops, and bank rules, all change the price of things a little bit each year. That's why your candy costs more than it did when Grandma was a kid!

ablations.prompt: Explain inflation to my 10-year-old cousin who asked why prices keep going up. Use exactly 3 bullet points, and write it at a grade 5 reading level or below.

runs.answer:
- Money loses some of its buying power over time. A dollar that bought a whole candy bar years ago might only buy half a candy bar today, because prices slowly climb.

- Lots of things push prices up. When more people want something than there is to go around, stores can charge more. Making things can also cost more, like when the price of sugar or gas goes up, and companies pass that cost on to you.

- Governments and banks watch prices closely. A little bit of price increase each year is normal, and they try to keep it slow and steady so money still works well for everyone.

- Money is worth less over time. Think of a dollar like a special ticket you use to buy things. When lots of people have lots of tickets, sellers can ask for more tickets for the same toy or snack, so prices go up.

- Things can get more expensive to make. If it costs more to get sugar, wood, or gas, the store has to charge more to stay in business.

- Prices rising slowly is normal. When prices go up a little each year, that's called inflation. Grown-ups at banks and governments watch it closely to keep it from getting too big.
